note: Scripts fed to the Chatterbox/CosyVoice ComfyUI workflow to synthesise the placeholder narration now sitting in public/audio/. One sentence per line, each line prefixed [Alice] - that is what the workflow expects to get natural phrasing, and it leans on the punctuation, so keep these grammatical if you re-record. Ids match the step ids in src/lib/tutorial.ts and src/lib/propertyTutorial.ts, and the mp3 for a step is public/audio/<tour>/<id>.mp3. These are PLACEHOLDERS: same voice as the eleven original clips, good enough to hear the whole tour end to end and judge pacing, not final takes.

tutorial.text:
[Alice] Light or dark, any time.
[Alice] This flips the whole app between light and dark mode whenever you like.
[Alice] It sticks until you tap it again.

[Alice] Try the refresh button, safely.
[Alice] Next to it, this icon reloads the app fresh if something ever looks stuck.
[Alice] Go ahead and press and hold it right now.
[Alice] It's just a preview while this tour is open, so nothing will actually be cleared.
[Alice] In real use, holding it for real does wipe this device's local cache and reload the page, though it never touches your saved inventory data.

[Alice] Find anything fast.
[Alice] Search by name, barcode, or location.
[Alice] Next to it, the sort menu can bump low-stock items straight to the top of the list.

[Alice] Bring in, or back up, a whole spreadsheet.
[Alice] Already track inventory in a spreadsheet?
[Alice] Import it here in one go.
[Alice] Export works the same way in reverse, any time you want a copy on hand.

[Alice] Sharing is caring.
[Alice] Send your saved barcode-to-item matches to a teammate, or pull in theirs.
[Alice] It's handy the first time you're both starting from scratch, so neither of you has to scan everything twice.

[Alice] A closer look at these icons.
[Alice] Over on the right, the icons cover breaking down a case, moving stock to another location, editing details, and deleting.
[Alice] Give each one a try, one at a time.

[Alice] Break down a case.
[Alice] Tap this icon to split a sealed case into individual units.
[Alice] It's handy the moment a case actually gets opened, so the count stays accurate at both levels.

[Alice] Edit the full details.
[Alice] The pencil opens this item's full details, including name, barcode, reorder point, usage tracking window, and more.

[Alice] Delete for good.
[Alice] And the trash icon removes an item entirely.
[Alice] It'll always ask you to confirm first, so there's no risk of an accidental tap losing anything.

[Alice] Two ways to log stock.
[Alice] Barcode mode is for one item at a time.
[Alice] Receipt mode reads a whole photographed receipt at once, which is great right after a big supply run.
[Alice] Accuracy can be hit or miss on a crumpled or blurry receipt, so it's worth a quick double-check of the results before trusting them completely.

[Alice] Choose how it searches, then where to buy.
[Alice] This toggle controls whether Find at searches by barcode or by name.
[Alice] Find at itself jumps straight to a search on a few common retailer sites.
[Alice] Give both a try.
[Alice] There's no rush, take whatever time you need.

[Alice] Jot down a tracking number.
[Alice] Once you've ordered, save the tracking number here for a quick link to the carrier's tracking page.
[Alice] It's simple by design, just a place to keep the number handy, not a live delivery tracker.

[Alice] Send the whole list to a supplier.
[Alice] Tap Share to text or email this entire reorder list straight to a supplier.
[Alice] That's everything currently at or below its reorder point, in one go.

[Alice] Zoom in or out on any time frame.
[Alice] These buttons switch the chart between a week, a month, a few months, or all-time.
[Alice] It's the fastest way to tell a one-off spike apart from a real ongoing trend.

[Alice] Push sends this device's copy up.
[Alice] If you connected Google Sheets a moment ago, go ahead and tap Push to Sheet now.
[Alice] It sends this device's current inventory up to your spreadsheet.
[Alice] Nothing syncs automatically.
[Alice] It only happens when you tap it.

[Alice] Put a name on your changes.
[Alice] Add your name here so teammates working the same inventory can see who made a change and when.
[Alice] It's just a label, not a login, and anyone on this device can update it.

[Alice] Pull brings it back down.
[Alice] And if you pushed earlier, tap Pull from Sheet now to bring that same inventory right back.
[Alice] That's proof your data really does live safely in the spreadsheet, not just on this one device.

[Alice] Track equipment, not just stock.
[Alice] Property is a separate space for tracking equipment and fixtures, including ordered parts and maintenance status.
[Alice] It syncs to its own tab on the same spreadsheet.

[Alice] Reminders, and a home-screen shortcut.
[Alice] Turn on daily reminders and you'll only hear from us when something's actually worth checking.
[Alice] And if you'd like this app to feel less like a browser tab, you can install it right to your home screen from here.

[Alice] Come back to this tour any time.
[Alice] This link brings this exact walkthrough back whenever you want a refresher.
[Alice] It's the only way to see it again now, since it no longer opens automatically.

[Alice] That's the tour!
[Alice] You're all set.
[Alice] Explore Inventory on your own from here, or tap Manage Property above to keep going with equipment tracking.

property.text:
[Alice] Syncs to its own tab, same sheet.
[Alice] Once Google Sheets is connected from the Account panel, Property gets its own Property tab on that same spreadsheet.
[Alice] Push sends this device's list there, and Pull brings it back.

[Alice] Add your own whenever you're ready.
[Alice] This button opens a short form, with name, location, serial number, and notes, for anything you want to track going forward.

[Alice] Edit the details any time.
[Alice] Tap Edit to update a property's name, location, serial number, or notes.
[Alice] Nothing here is locked in once it's added.

[Alice] Or just set the status directly.
[Alice] Logging a receipt isn't the only way to move a part along.
[Alice] This dropdown lets you jump straight to Ordered, Shipped, Received, Installed, or Cancelled whenever that's a better fit.

[Alice] Add a part right from here.
[Alice] Type or scan a part number to look it up, or just fill in the description yourself.
[Alice] Quantity, price, and an expected delivery date are all optional.

[Alice] Track maintenance the same way.
[Alice] Type a repair or maintenance job here and hit enter to add it to the list.
[Alice] Its own status and history work exactly like an ordered part's.

[Alice] Come back to this tour any time.
[Alice] This link brings this exact walkthrough back whenever you want a refresher.

[Alice] That's Property tracking!
[Alice] Delete the example with this icon whenever you're ready, then add your own.
[Alice] When you're done, close this with the X up in the corner.
